why_company.draft:
ChowNow's role is attractive because it is unusually explicit about what good operations should do: Find the friction, define what actually needs to change, translate the business need into a buildable requirement, and reduce the manual burden on Sales and Customer Success.

That matches how I have approached post-sales operations.  At Check Point, I built workflows across Salesforce, Custify, and Jira, improved portfolio visibility from roughly 40% to 99%, and supported a coverage model that reached 99% dedicated CSM coverage for accounts above $50K.  I have also managed customer portfolios directly, which gives me a practical view of when a field, workflow, health score, or report helps the team and when it simply creates more administrative work.

I am also drawn to the full lifecycle scope of this role.  It includes pipeline and handoff discipline, onboarding stages and SLAs, customer health, segmentation, capacity planning, retention, win-back logic, and CRM hygiene.  Those pieces work best when they are designed as one connected operating model rather than a collection of separate processes.

I would bring a systems-literate operator's perspective to ChowNow: Start from what the rep or post-sales team needs to decide, define the cleanest process and data contract, and partner with Business Systems to make that behavior durable.

cover_letter.draft:
Dear ChowNow Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Sales & Customer Success Operations Manager role because the position is centered on a problem I have repeatedly solved: Turning messy customer-facing workflows into clear operating rules, useful reporting, and scalable handoffs.

At Check Point, I built and improved workflows across Salesforce, Custify, and Jira, helped move portfolio visibility from roughly 40% to 99%, and supported 99% dedicated CSM coverage for accounts above $50K.  I also managed 20 to 40 SaaS accounts totaling approximately $3M ARR, so I understand the downstream cost when stages, handoffs, health logic, or CRM data do not match how the team actually works.

The breadth of ChowNow's role is especially relevant to me.  I have worked across onboarding, adoption, retention, escalation, portfolio management, reporting, and process improvement.  At Dedrone, I standardized enterprise onboarding to about one month while engagement increased 25% and renewals increased 20%.  I have also used automation to reduce repetitive work and improve handoffs, including Salesforce-to-Jira workflow patterns.

I would approach ChowNow's Sales and CS Operations work by making lifecycle definitions explicit, identifying the minimum data needed for each decision, defining clear ownership and acceptance criteria, and then partnering closely with Business Systems on the technical implementation.

I have also built a synthetic candidate CRM for this role through Clintware to model the lifecycle, health, onboarding, capacity, and risk logic described in the public job posting.  It is proof of how I think, not a claim about ChowNow's private systems.

Clinton Kosh
